A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECI sampling research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ECI generation and regression experiments in Tables 3–6, with additional evaluations and ablations in Appendix E. Table 5 explicitly distinguishes the borrowed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original ECI experimental results, including PDE generation, regression, efficiency measurements, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–5 retain the same extrapolation, correction, interpolation, mixing, and noise-resampling procedures. Appendix A.3 changes terminology and the projection description, but the displayed correction updates remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Stokes, heat, Darcy, Navier–Stokes, porous-medium, and Stefan systems. The generative, regression, superresolution, and varying-constraint scenarios in Tables 2 and 7 and Appendix E are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: ANP, ProbConserv, DiffusionPDE, D-Flow, CondFFM, and the relevant FFM/FNO references. Table 5 retains ANP, SoftC-ANP, HardC-ANP, and ProbConserv. The revised DiffusionPDE wording does not change its evaluated adaptation.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, resolutions, model configurations, solver settings, and evaluation metrics are unchanged in Tables 2, 4, and 7 and Appendices B–D. No new experiment or revised evaluation design is reported.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same mixing/resampling sweeps, prior-checkpoint ablation, varying-constraint evaluations, per-frame Navier–Stokes analysis, and constraint-information study. Section 4.3 and Appendix E retain their questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain 512 generated samples for 2D evaluations and 100 for 3D evaluations, Gaussian log-likelihood reporting, and the 3σ predictive intervals in Figure 17. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The result entries in Tables 3–6 and 8–11 match, including ECI's Stokes-IC FPD of 0.076 and Navier–Stokes FPD of 1.131 in Table 3. Corresponding figures preserve the reported patterns; their visual refinements do not introduce new findings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 changes the stated mathematical characterization of correction from orthogonal to oblique projection. This is a limited descriptive revision: the correction formulas, constraint equations, measure-theoretic definitions, and Proposition 1 with its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Despite the broader title, both abstracts, introductions, and conclusions make the same substantive claims about unified gradient-free guidance, exact hard constraints, PDE generation quality, efficiency, and competitive zero-shot regression.

C2.justification: The interpretations of variance control, baseline artifacts, regression confidence, and task-dependent hyperparameters remain unchanged. The region-constraint terminology and revised DiffusionPDE loss-minimization wording clarify distinctions already present without establishing new applicability boundaries or limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. This adds code-access information; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and data-generation disclosures in Appendices B–D are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Reference reflow, citation punctuation, and grammatical corrections do not add literature or revise the paper's novelty relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: The title becomes Gradient-Free Generation for Hard-Constrained Systems, affiliations are updated, and scattered grammar and explanatory wording are refined. Appendix A.3 and Algorithm 5 adopt region-constraint terminology. The narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR title, heading, and running-header formatting. Existing heatmaps receive larger color-bar labels, adjusted ticks, and spacing refinements; Figure 1 is restyled and some floats move. All 22 figures and 11 tables retain their basic organization, with small caption corrections.

improvement.justification: v2 improves usability through clearer color-bar labels, small language and caption corrections, and an explicit code-access link. These are concrete but limited gains: the experimental evidence, correction formulas, proof, and principal limitations remain unchanged.
